topics.title: West Coast water pulse raises flood worries
topics.summary: Forecasters say warm Pacific Kelvin waves could lift West Coast sea levels by up to a foot this month, increasing erosion and nuisance flooding risks through winter.
topics.discussionPrompt: If the ocean starts acting extra dramatic for months, who checks the tide charts and who just moves the beach picnic inland?

topics.title: Supreme Court takes climate-fire case
topics.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court will hear a major climate case tied to Colorado's Marshall Fire, with governments seeking damages over fossil fuel companies' alleged role in warming.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a lawsuit tries to connect climate change to one disaster, who wants accountability and who worries courts are being asked to do too much?

topics.title: Voters frustrated with both parties
topics.summary: An AP-NORC poll found voters favor Democrats on several issues but still lack confidence that either major party can solve the country's biggest problems.
topics.discussionPrompt: When people dislike both teams but still have to vote, who becomes the practical chooser and who starts inventing a third option over coffee?

topics.title: Brazil campaign tests global alliances
topics.summary: Brazil's tight presidential race is drawing international attention as candidates spar over sovereignty, security and relations with the United States ahead of Sunday's vote.
topics.discussionPrompt: If another country's election could shift global politics, who follows every poll and who admits they're mostly trying to learn the basics?

topics.title: Spain protests over housing squeeze
topics.summary: More than 50 housing protests were scheduled across Spain after parliament rejected emergency measures, keeping pressure on leaders over rents and affordability.
topics.discussionPrompt: When housing gets too expensive, who blames slow politics, who blames the market, and who just wants a place with decent sunlight?

topics.title: Kyiv bridges hit by new disruption tactic
topics.summary: Russian aerial strikes snarled traffic on three Kyiv bridges, a disruption Ukraine described as part of a broader effort to pressure the capital's daily life.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a city keeps functioning under pressure, who notices the logistics first and who notices how stubborn everyday routines can be?

topics.title: G7 plans emergency fuel release
topics.summary: G7 leaders agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves after fuel prices jumped and Washington pressed allies to act.
topics.discussionPrompt: When governments tap emergency fuel reserves, who sees smart crisis management and who wonders what happens after the cushion is gone?

topics.title: Rare ibises follow human-led migration
topics.summary: A conservation project is guiding rare northern bald ibises across Europe, using human pilots to help the birds relearn a migration route.
topics.discussionPrompt: If humans have to teach birds an old route, who finds that beautiful and who asks how anyone got the birds to trust the plan?

topics.title: Victoria quake shakes Melbourne area
topics.summary: A magnitude 4.8 earthquake struck Victoria, with tremors felt around Melbourne and residents reporting shaking across parts of southeastern Australia.
topics.discussionPrompt: After a surprise tremor, who calmly checks the news and who immediately becomes the building's unofficial earthquake expert?

topics.title: Verstappen grabs first 2026 pole
topics.summary: Max Verstappen took his and Red Bull's first pole position of the 2026 Formula One season, setting up a high-interest race weekend in Malaysia.
topics.discussionPrompt: When one big qualifying lap changes the mood of a season, who starts making predictions and who refuses to jinx anything?
